name: Lightbringer
description:
Requires Attunement.

Before attunement it looks like a Club: Melee(STR), light, 1d4 bludgeoning
After attunement (while it lasts) this weapon can morhp into a:
 - Mace: Melee(STR), 1d6 bludgeoning
 - Morningstar: Melee(STR), 1d8 piercing
or remain a club, based on in which weapon is the owner proficient (if more than one, it morhpes to the highest damage).
Also, while attuned, the wielder has a +1 bonus to both hit chance and damage rolls.

While attuned, the wielder can command the weapon to glow, giving off faint light in a 20 ft. radius.
While glowing, it has extra 1d6 damage against undead creatures.

In the hilt of the weapon the holy simbol of Lathander, the god of dawn, is implanted like a pommel. If the wielder is a follower of another god of the Light or Fire domain, the symbol will morph into that god's, while attuned.

name: Dragonguard Chestplate
description:
Medium Armor (breastplate, AC: 14 + dex mod, max 2)

While wearing this armor you have +1 AC, and you have advantage on saving throws against any breath weapon attacks, and an additional +1 on saving throws against fire based attacks.

name: Gauntlets of Ogre Power
description: Your Strength score is 19 while you wear these gauntlets. They have no effect on you if your Strength is 19 or higher without them.

name: Staff of the Python
description:
Quarterstaff: Melee(STR), versatile: 1d6/1d8 bludgeoning

Requires attunement.

You can use an action to speak this staff's command word and throw the staff on the ground within 10 feet of you. The staff becomes a giant constrictor snake under your control and acts on its own initiative count. By using a bonus action to speak the command word again, you return the staff to its normal form in a space formerly occupied by the snake.

On your turn, you can mentally command the snake if it is within 60 feet of you and you aren't incapacitated. You decide what action the snake takes and where it moves during its next turn, or you can issue it a general command, such as to attack your enemies or guard a location. If the snake is reduced to 0 hit points, it dies and reverts to its staff form. The staff then shatters and is destroyed. If the snake reverts to staff form before losing all its hit points, it regains all of them.

name: Daggermaster's Ring
description:
Requires Attunement

All attacks made with daggers have a +2 chance to hit, and you can decide wether the damage will be magical or not.

Nat19 also ensures a critical hit.

name: Decanter of Endless Water
description:
You can use an action to remove the stopper and speak one of three command words, whereupon an amount of fresh water or salt water (your choice) pours out of the flask. The water stops pouring out at the start of your next turn. Choose from the following options:
 - "Stream" produces 1 gallon of water
 - "Fountain" produces 5 gallons of water.
 - "Geyser" produces 30 gallons of water that gushes forth in a geyser 30 feet long and 1 foot wide.

As a bonus action while holding the decanter, you can aim the geyser at a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or take 1d4 bludgeoning damage and fall prone.

Instead of a creature, you can target an object that isn't being worn or carried and that weighs no more than 200 pounds. The object is either knocked over or pushed up to 15 feet away from you.

name: Bag of Tricks
description:
This ordinary bag appears empty. Reaching inside the bag, however, reveals the presence of a small, fuzzy object. You can use an action to pull the fuzzy object from the bag and throw it up to 20 feet. When the object lands, it transforms into a creature you determine by rolling a d8 and consulting the list below.

The creature is friendly to you and your companions, and it acts on your turn. You can use a bonus action to command how the creature moves and what action it takes on its next turn, or to give it general orders, such as to attack your enemies. In the absence of such orders, the creature acts in a fashion appropriate to its nature. Once three fuzzy objects have been pulled from the bag, the bag can't be used again until the next dawn.

1 - Weasel,
2 - Owl,
3 - Badger,
4 - Boar,
5 - Panther,
6 - Ape,
7 - Dire Wolf,
8-Black Bear

name: Robe of Useful Items
description:
This robe has cloth patches of various shapes and colors covering it.

While wearing the robe, you can use an action to detach one of the patches, causing it to become the object or creature it represents. Once the last patch is removed, the robe becomes an ordinary garment.

This robe contains the following patches:

-Lantern (lit, filled)
-Rowboat (4 person)
-Hemphen rope (50 ft, coiled)
-2 wooden ladders (25 ft)
-Iron chest (3ft x 4ft, 2 ft deep, empty)

name: Googles of Night
description: While wearing these dark lenses, you have Darkvision out to 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, wearing the goggles increases its range by 60 feet.

name: Stone of Good Luck
description:
Requires Attunement.

While this polished agate is on your person, you gain a +1 bonus to ability checks and saving throws.

name: Bottled Breath
description:
A transparent vial conatining a breathful of elemental air.

When you inhale it you can chose from tho following two options:
-Exhale immediately: You cast the Gust of Wind spell
-Hold it: You don't have to breathe for up until 1 hour. You may end this effect early (e.g. for speaking) but that do not grant you the benefit of the Exhale option.

name: Alchemy Jug
description:
This ceramic jug appears to be able to hold a 5 litres of liquid and weighs 5 kilos whether full or empty. Sloshing sounds can be heard from within the jug when it is shaken, even if the jug is empty.

You can use an action and name one liquid from the list below to cause the jug to produce the chosen liquid. Afterward, you can uncork the jug as an action and pour that liquid out, up to 10 litres per minute. The maximum amount of liquid the jug can produce depends on the liquid you named. Once the jug starts producing a liquid, it can't produce a different one, or more of one that has reached its maximum, until the next dawn.

Available liquids:
Honey (0.25 litre),
Cooking oil (1 litre),
Lamp oil (0.5 litre),
Vinegar (10 litre),
Soy Sauce (5 litre),
Salt water (60 litre),
Beer (5 litre),
Wine (5 litre)

name: Wand of the Warmage
description:
Requires attunement by a spellcaster.

Club: Melee(STR), light, 1d4 bludgeoning

While holding this wand, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls. In addition, you ignore Half Cover when making a spell atack roll.

name: Javellin of Lightning
description:
Javellin: Melee(STR), thrown (30/120), 1d6 piercing

When you hurl it and speak its command word, it transforms into a bolt of lightning, forming a line 5 feet wide that extends out from you to a target within 120 feet. Each creature in the line excluding you and the target must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d6 lightning damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The lightning bolt turns back into a javelin when it reaches the target. Make a ranged weapon attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes damage from the javelin plus 4d6 lightning damage. The javellin's lighning property can't be used again until the next dawn. In the meantime, the javellin can still be used as a magic weapon with basic javellin stats.

name: Amulet of the Drunkard
description:
This amulet smells of old, ale-stained wood.

While wearing it, you can regain 4d4 + 4 hit points when you drink a pint (0.5 litre) of beer, ale, mead, or wine. Once the amulet has restored hit points, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Dried Leech
description:
This leech has been dried and imbued with a mote of animating magic. If you hit a creature with a ranged attack roll using this ammunition, the leech springs to life and sinks its teeth into the target, dealing 1d8 piercing damage at the start of each of the target’s turns.

If the leech deals at least 30 damage or the target dies, the leech falls off.

A creature, including the target, can use its action to detach the leech, but detaching it causes 1d6 additional damage and inflicts the bleed condition for 2 turns.

Once a leech is no longer attached to its target, the leech dies and is no longer magical.

name: Box of Paper Birds
description:
A box containing 7 magical sheets of paper.

After you write a message of fifty words or fewer on one of the papers, and speak a creature's name, the parchment magically folds into a Tiny paper bird and flies to the recipient whose name you uttered.

The recipient must be on the same plane of existence as you, otherwise the bird turns into ash as it takes flight. It travels to within 5 feet of its intended recipient by the most direct route, with a 60 ft flying speed, whereupon it turns into a nonmagical and inanimate sheet of parchment that can be unfolded only by the intended recipient.

If the bird's hit points or speed is reduced to 0 or if it is otherwise immobilized, it turns into ash.

name: Packets of Pixie Dust
description:
3 small packets of pixie dust wrapped together.

As an action, you can sprinkle this dust on yourself or another creature you can see within 5 feet of you. The recipient gains a flying speed of 30 feet and the ability to hover for 1 minute.

If the creature is airborne when this effect ends, it falls safely to the ground, taking no damage and landing on its feet.

name: Sending Stone
description:
Sending stones come in pairs, with each smooth stone carved to match the other so the pairing is easily recognized.

While you touch one stone, you can use an action to cast the sending spell from it. The target is the bearer of the other stone. If no creature bears the other stone, you know that fact as soon as you use the stone and don't cast the spell. Once sending is cast through the stones, they can't be used again until the next dawn.

If one of the stones in a pair is destroyed, the other one becomes nonmagical.

name: Spider Staff
description:
Quasrterstaff: Melee(STR), Versatile, 1d6 opne hand, 1d8 two hand, bludgeoning.

Requires Attunement

While attuned, it deals 1d6 extra poison damage as a melee weapon.

The staff has 10 charges, which are used to fuel the spells within it. With the staff in hand, you can use your action to cast one of the following spells from the staff:
-spider climb (1 charge)
-web (2 charges, spell save DC 15).
No components are required. The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges each day at dusk.

If you expend the staff’s last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the staff crumbles to dust and is destroyed.

name: Dragoncrest Medalion
description:
A silvery-looking medallion etched with a dragon motif. Its surface becomes warm to the touch when divine magic is nearby.

While wearing this medallion, you can see a small, spectral, salamander-like lizard resting on your shoulder. It seems friendly and playful, but only you can see or hear it, and it never leaves you. It appears clear and bright when the medalion is fully charged and becomes more and more dim, and hazy as the charges are used.

The medalion is linked to your divine energy, having a maximum charge capacity equal to half your level, rounded down. You can regain 1d4+1 charges after a long rest. You can use 1 charge per turn in combat as a bonus action or reaction:
- If you miss with a spell attack, you may add +2 to the roll, potentially turning the miss into a hit.
- When hit by an area attack, you gain advantage on the saving throw.

name: Boots of the Vigilant Wing
description:
You gain a +1 bonus to AC while not wearing heavy or light armor.

Once per long rest, when you would be hit by an attack, you may use your reaction to move 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks, potentially causing the attack to miss.

name: Bulwark of the Iron Will
description:
Shield (AC+2)

A heavy steel shield etched with angular patterns resembling chains and fortress walls. It feels unnervingly solid.

While wielding this shield, when you succeed on a saving throw against an attack, you may use your reaction to gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

Once per long rest, when you would be pushed, knocked prone, or moved against your will, you may ignore the effect.

name: Banner of the Iron Vanguard
description:
A big red ribbon with golden lining that can be worn around heavy armor distinguishing the wearer.

Once per short rest, you can activate the magic of the fabric, granting one target ally (including yourself) to have +2 to any Charisma based ability checks in the next 10 minutes.

name: Silk Gloves of the Kindled Hand
description:
Fine crimson silk gloves embroidered with golden flame motifs. They are warm, no matter the temperature outside.

While wearing the gloves, when you restore hit points to a single creature using a spell of 1st level or higher, you may add +1d4 healing (once per turn).

Also once per long rest, when you cast a healing spell, you may also end one minor condition on the target (blinded, deafened, or poisoned, etc.).

name: Censer of Sustained Flame
description:
A small censer, with a little chain that can be attached to your belt, or to the grip of a weapon. When lit, it burns with a smokeless, golden fire, giving off scent of fresh campfire.

As an action or bonus action, once per short or long rest, you can light the censer for 10 minutes. While it is burning, allies within 15 feet of you, including you, get +1 for any ability check or saving throw. The effect diminishes during the heat of combat.

The censer sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius.

name: Golden Ring of the Apprentices
description:
Requires attunement.

A small golden ring that only fits your little finger. It is usually given to magic apprentices who can not managed their spells well.

Once during a short or long rest a spell caster can perform a quick ritual that stores a single spell they know into the ring. Only the attuned user can release the spell, unless the ring is destroyed, in which case the stored spell is released automatically.

If someone tries to store a spell while the ring already stores one, the spell acts like it was cast normally, but treating the ring as the target or center of effect.

The stored spell can be released as an action, regardless of the stored spell. It gain statistics (save DC, etc) based on the original caster, who stored the spell at the time of casting.

name: Lens of Revealing Threads
description:
A monocle on a chain.

While examining an area or object through the lens, you gain advantage on Investigation checks regarding that object.

Once per day, you may focus strongly on your surroundings to see if objects have faint magical auras on them or not (as a limited detect magic).

name: Earrings of Misdirected Attention
description:
A mismatched pair of small silver earrings that gently chime once in a while despite no apparent reason for them to make that sound. Also it seems only you can hear that chime, though it never happens when you are alone.

Once per short rest, when a creature you can see within 30 feet makes a Wisdom or Intelligence save, you may use your reaction to impose disadvantage on that save. If the save fails, you gain advantage on your next Stealth or Sleight of Hand check against that creature.

name: Fedora of the Quiet Step
description:
A classic, detective-like hat from soft linen.

You gain advantage on Stealth checks made in dim light or darkness. Once you are in hiding, your own footsteps can never give you away.

When you step one feet over a hole or chasm, or other fissure you would fall into, you do not fall yet. If your next step lands on solid ground, it would seem that you somehow jumped over. If this can not be done, you fall down, and everyone will see it like you jumped down on purpose.

name: Mantle of the Shared Decay
description:
A cloak woven from fungus-thread and decorated with shed leaves.

The cloak helps you guide your Halo of Spores around, so the following rules apply to any creature in the halo:
-When a creature fails a saving throw against one of your spells, you may choose one ally (including yourself) within 10 feet of it to gain advantage on their next attack or saving throw against that creature (once per turn).
-Once per short or long rest, when a creature succeeds on a saving throw against one of your druid spells, you may impose a –2 penalty to that save (before the result is finalized)
-Once per short or long rest, when you make a spell attack roll against any target that is or was in your halo since your last turn, and you miss, you may add +1d4 to the roll potentially changing the result.

name: Boots of the Rooted Step
description:
These boots sprout thin rootlets when touching soil or stone.

Once per short or long rest, you can cast a root field as a bonus action. The center of the field must be within 20 feet of you, and it will have a diameter of 40 feet. The field counts as a difficult terrain for everyone except you, and hurts any creature who is not you by 1d4+1 if they start their turn in the field. The field disintegrates in 1 minute, but otherwise counts as a natural object unaffected by dispel magic.

While standing in the field, you have the following benefits:
-Advantage on saving throws against being knocked prone or moved
-Ability to exclude any creature of your choice from the negative effects of the field
-You can help any other creature fallen prone in the field to recover as a free action.

name: Boots of the Rooted Step
description:
A leaf-patterned cloak that seems half a second out of sync with reality.

Once per round, when a creature misses you with a melee attack, you may move 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

Once per short or long rest, when you take damage, you may teleport 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

name: Bracers of Reactive Misdirection
description:
Slender wooden bracers carved with spirals and thorn motifs.

When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you may use your reaction to impose disadvantage on that attack if you moved at least 10 feet on your last turn.

When a creature moves at least 10 feet toward you, ending in melee range to you, you may use your reaction to gain 10 feet of movement on your next turn. This movement won't trigger an opportunity attack from that enemy.

name: Feymark Compass
description:
A small crystal disk worn on a cord, but it does not seem to show North at all.

Once per long or short rest, at the start of a turn in combat (as highest initiative) you may swap initiative order with one willing ally you can see.
